# Demo script (2:48, one story)

*Generated by `scripts/make_video.py` from the same table that drives the recording and the subtitles.*

**One story:** a caregiver delegates her mother's shopping to an assistant. The seven things on screen (limits,
signature, purchase, refusal, dispute, proof, revoke) are the same product seen from one person's side.

The recording is silent on purpose, with burned-in captions in `docs/demo/`. **Record your own voice**: judges
should hear a person, and a synthetic voice reads as filler. About 247 words, about 88 words per minute
at this pacing, so read it a little briskly or trim a sentence per segment.

| Time | On screen | Say |
|---|---|---|
| 00:00 | Buyer app, top of the page. | Imagine your mum shops through an AI assistant. One poisoned product review could talk it into spending her money. Agents can pay. Mandate lets them prove they were allowed to. |
| 00:12 | Pick the Family caregiver situation, press Turn into limits. | I say what her assistant may buy: household essentials, under thirty dollars, one approved store, one week. Mandate turns that into limits, and if I leave one out it asks me instead of guessing. |
| 00:34 | Press Sign this mandate. | I sign it. That creates a credential chain. The assistant can only spend inside it, and the PayPal order will carry the hash of that chain. |
| 00:45 | Buy for me, approve, capture, open the signed receipt. | The assistant buys a night light. I approve, it captures, and I get a receipt that is signed and tied to my mandate. In this demo PayPal is a simulator; the real sandbox runs with your own keys. |
| 01:09 | Simulate a hijacked agent; the Refused slip appears. | Now a review hides an instruction to buy something she never allowed. This agent obeys it. The guard refuses and shows why. The model proposes; plain code decides. |
| 01:41 | Open a dispute, then the console: fault split, decision, evidence note, injection message. | A buyer opens a dispute. The dispute agent applies a published rule, builds an evidence packet and decides. Sandbox outcomes are scripted, so I claim no win rate. And a message telling it to refund is flagged for a human. |
| 02:13 | Audit log, Verify the whole chain, then the Mandate-Bench tab. | Every decision lands in a hash-chained log you can verify. And the benchmark: scripted attackers, two hundred and ninety attacks, none get through the full system. That is synthetic. A real-model run is one command. |
| 02:39 | Back to the buyer app, Revoke. | One switch ends the authority and returns what was not delivered. Mandate. Open source, Apache two. |

Join your recording to the picture:

```bash
ffmpeg -i docs/demo/mandate-demo-silent.mp4 -i voice.m4a -c:v copy -c:a aac -shortest mandate-demo-final.mp4
```

What the video says out loud so nobody has to discover it later: PayPal is simulated unless you bring sandbox
keys; dispute outcomes are scripted; the benchmark is synthetic. Upload it as a public YouTube video and keep
the title free of the word "sandbox-proven": it is not.

To redo the picture after a UI change: `python scripts/make_video.py`.
